title: Sails & Safeguards — Q4 Wrap (All-hands)
customer_attendees: Leadership team: Elena Park (CEO), Jonah Reed (CTO), Priya Nair (VP Product)
summary: Quarter-end all-hands focused on operational resilience, product milestones, compliance progress, hiring runway, and a short Q&A. Leadership provided highlights, risk posture, and concrete next steps for teams.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 | Time: 16:00 PST | Duration: ~42m | Location: All-hands virtual
Attendees: company-wide All Hands (leadership on stage)

[00:00:05] Elena Park (CEO): okay everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining the quarter wrap, we're gonna keep this tight 40-ish minutes, a lot to cover, so first up quick scoreboard.
[00:00:22] Elena: Q4 revenue is up 28% quarter over quarter, usage growth strong particularly in embeddings and streaming generation, thanks to the infra teams for the latency improvements. uh applause emoji.
[00:00:35] Jonah Reed (CTO): yeah quick tech note — we've rolled the new kernel scheduler to 3 more regions last week, and the latency p50 dropped by about 12% on our 2-stage benchmarks. Some noise on long-tail p99 remains — that's due to KV cache eviction storms on multi-tenant hosts. we're diagnosing.
[00:01:03] Priya Nair (VP Product): on product, we shipped structured output templates and expanded function-calling defaults; adoption is at 18% of generation calls now, which is ahead of our plan. That helps both developer ergonomics and downstream cost.
[00:01:25] Marcus Lee (Head of Eng): To add, the Dedicated rollout for the new autoscaler is live on beta accounts. We hit a few edge cases for burst-to-zero and the scheduler misfired on certain policy configs, which resulted in some brief throttling for a customer — postmortem in Confluence.
[00:01:50] Sofia Alvarez (Head of People): hiring update — we made 42 offers this quarter, onboarding mostly across infra and customer success; attrition is within targeted bands but we have a manager hiring freeze in a couple of teams while we finalize org realignments.
[00:02:10] Elena: thank you. next section: risk & security. Tariq, quick on compliance.
[00:02:16] Tariq Banerjee (Security): SOC 2 scope expansion is on track, control testing started this week, and ISO audit scheduling is tentatively set for early Q1. note: the VPC/on-prem checklist was slightly out of date, we pushed an internal patch and will publish an updated runbook by next week. passwordless auth rollout for internal tools is in progress but delayed by one sprint due to SAML provider changes.
[00:02:45] Audience (crosstalk): (murmur) 
[00:02:50] Elena: okay, operational incidents — Marcus?
[00:02:55] Marcus: couple of incidents to call out: one customer saw repeated timeouts when a regional shard hit full memory due to KV cache growth after a large chat session. mitigation was rolling a larger instance, then we tuned the eviction threshold. second was a deploy that pushed a bad quantization profile causing hallucination regression in a small subset of models — rollback and tighter canary thresholds fixed it.
[00:03:25] Marcus: takeaways — we need better chaos testing for multi-tenant KV cache, and more automated canary gates on quantization profiles.
[00:03:35] Priya: product note — we will add model-level quality checks tied to evaluation suites so any quantization change triggers diffs on our core prompts. devs can opt-out if they have valid reason but should be rare.
[00:03:55] Elena: good. now on go-to-market and customers.
[00:04:00] Jonah: we ran three benchmark engagements this quarter—one public, two private. Public benchmark shows us at parity with competitive offerings on cost/throughput for 8k context models, with faster startup latency in our hosted paths. private benchmarks highlighted a simple pattern: customers with large batch inference benefit most from Dedicated with predictive batching.
[00:04:28] Elena: we had an interesting ask from finance vertical — they wanted stronger data residency controls plus HSM-backed KMS. Tariq, ETA?
[00:04:36] Tariq: HSM integration is in design, prototype with our KMS partner next sprint. Data residency options—we have region pinning but need formal contracts + audit support for legal. will have a deck for sales next week.
[00:04:52] Audience question (typed): what about Private on-prem roadmap?
[00:04:55] Jonah: Private continues to be a priority — we've simplified the installer for air-gapped installs and we're working on better telemetry that doesn't exfiltrate customer data; aim to add easier rollback in the 1.2 release.
[00:05:12] Elena: great. switching to finance and runway briefly.
[00:05:15] Elena: spend discipline is in effect; marketing and hiring levers will be reviewed, but we are not cutting core infra spend. we want to ensure reliability targets are met before scaling much more.
[00:05:30] Sofia: compensation cycles are proceeding; we plan adjustments in Q1 and are evaluating equity refresh guidelines. more to come in town halls with managers.
[00:05:44] Elena: next: product launches and developer experience. Priya?
[00:05:48] Priya: upcoming launches — fine-grained routing policies for model variants (this reduces cost by steering non-critical traffic to cheaper quantized variants), an insights dashboard to surface per-route cost and latency, and a new onboarding CLI that reduces time-to-first-call by about 40% in alpha.
[00:06:12] Elena: thanks. I want to call out the customer stories — large retail customer did a feature launch using Redwood Dedicated and their SLA improved X, they cited our autoscaling as a key enabler.
[00:06:26] Marcus: small note — please stop using 'kayvee cache' in docs, it's KV cache, but we sometimes see 'kay-v' in transcripts which confuses folks.
[00:06:37] (laughter)
[00:06:40] Elena: ha, noted. community & open-model partnerships — Jonah?
[00:06:44] Jonah: We're sponsoring an open-model workshop in January, and our model onboarding toolkit is being open-sourced next month. this should increase inbound model contributions and help downstream evals.
[00:06:58] Elena: important for our thesis — serving wins over model ownership, but we still want strong community signals.
[00:07:06] Audience Q&A segment begins.
[00:07:10] Attendee: hi — any changes to PTO or remote work policy?
[00:07:13] Sofia: no changes this quarter. we are standardizing manager calibrations and expect more granularity on flexible work in the new handbook.
[00:07:22] Attendee: can you talk about redundancy across regions? we saw some slowdowns earlier.
[00:07:26] Jonah: redundancy is multi-region with cross-region fallback for most models; the sticky part is cache warm-up when routing flips — working on adaptive pre-warming heuristics.
[00:07:40] Attendee: on the security side, any update on penetration testing cadence?
[00:07:44] Tariq: annual pentests continue, and we've added a quarterly internal red-team focused on access controls; results are in the security channel.
[00:07:55] Elena: okay, we'll move to the tactical ask/next-steps portion.
[00:08:00] Elena: quick recap of decisions — keep hiring for infra and cs, pause some manager hires til org changes, accelerate HSM proof-of-concept, prioritize canary gating, and publish updated VPC/on-prem runbook.
[00:08:16] Marcus: also engineering will adopt a stricter release window for quantization changes and add synthetic load tests for KV cache failure modes.
[00:08:26] Priya: product will roll out the model-level eval hooks to staging by Dec 10.
[00:08:33] Elena: alright, final section is shoutouts and wins.
[00:08:37] Sofia: shoutout to the infra team for the region kernel rollouts, and CS for an excellent Q4 renewal close.
[00:08:45] (applause, clapping)
[00:08:50] Elena: thanks team. closing housekeeping: we will circulate the deck, post the detailed action-item list, and run skip-level town halls next week.
[00:09:02] Elena: ok — open mic for two more questions.
[00:09:06] Attendee: will there be more transparency in platform costs for teams?
[00:09:09] Priya: yes — the insights dashboard will expose cost per route and per model, launching in beta to platform teams first.
[00:09:18] Attendee: any immediate changes to incident communication?
[00:09:21] Marcus: we'll shorten the incident notification window and add a short-form incident digest on the #status channel.
[00:09:28] Audience (murmurs)
[00:09:35] Elena: thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.
